title: Pechenegs (Pecinaci)
fact_summary: A people that two of the written sources on this map name as the ones who drove the Hungarians from their earlier homes.

claims.text: Regino of Prüm, under 889, says the Hungarians were driven from their own homes by neighbouring peoples “qui Pecinaci vocantur”.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the source says. The passage was read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: Chapter 38 of the Byzantine De Administrando Imperio says the Pechenegs fell upon the Turks (the Hungarians) and drove them out together with their prince Árpád.
claims.certainty_reason: Read only as Tóth quotes the chapter.

open_questions.text: Regino in the West and the emperor's informants in Constantinople both blame the Pechenegs. Did they hear the same story, or independent ones?

review.note: Checked by Claude against open copies of every source. Marc spot-checks a sample.
